prose: President Trump said Tuesday he signed a 'morally binding' AI document with tech leaders after a White House luncheon, telling reporters he is seeing 'tremendous self-policing' and that the administration is considering a 10-person committee to oversee the AI industry. House Speaker Mike Johnson called the agreement a voluntary statement of principles. Outside, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei said risk rules are still under discussion, as Washington debates intensify alongside mounting agent-orchestrated attacks.
highlights: Trump signs what he calls a 'morally binding' AI accord with tech leaders
Administration weighing a 10-person committee to oversee the AI industry
Mike Johnson: the principles are 'voluntary on behalf of the industry'
Trump cites 'tremendous self-policing' by tech companies
Amodei: rules addressing AI risks 'still under discussion'
